Hi Priyom / Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — BlueNorth's compliance team asked us to share a short list of must-have signals for our pilot. High level asks: full ingest-level audit for chat/embedding requests (request headers + tokenized length), a 90-day retention window for logs, and the ability to require customer-managed keys for workspace-level data export.

A couple of clarifying Qs we couldn't answer in the call:
- Can audit exports be scoped to a single workspace ID so we can keep dev/test separate?
- If CMK is required, will the export pipeline keep logs encrypted with the customer key or re-encrypt with Redwoods' keys for long-term storage?
- For SSO activity, they want a mapping of SAML assertions to user_id in logs — is that in the current schema?

We have an internal deadline to lock the pilot acceptance criteria by Nov 20. Appreciate any notes or a one-page summary you can share.

Best,
Lydia

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai; marissa.cole@redwood.ai; soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Audit capture questions ahead of pilot

Forwarding BlueNorth's asks — priority: workspace-scoped exports, CMK behavior, SSO assertion mapping.

Thoughts:
- Workspace scoping: our current export API supports a workspace_id filter, but the audit ledger still stores tenant_id at the record level; need to confirm RBAC rules for who can request the export.
- CMK: per our initial design, we encrypt logs at rest with a per-tenant envelope key that is wrapped by our service key. Supporting CMK end-to-end for export will require adding a KMS-wrap option during export time (needs vault changes).
- SSO mapping: we already capture SAML Subject and NameID in the auth event, but we don't consistently persist a canonical user_id in the same audit row for all services — that's the gap BlueNorth hit on.

I'm tagging Marissa and Soojin for product/ops and infra impact. We need a short workback and decision: ship minimal export + doc for pilot, or delay until CMK full-path and canonical user_id are in place. Options and ETA please — BlueNorth wants acceptance criteria by 11/20.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Security PM, Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick technical summary and tradeoffs below so we can pick a path.

1) Workspace-scoped export
- Current state: export endpoint supports workspace_id and filters; export job runs into the audit S3 bucket with envelope encryption using our service KMS.
- Risk: If we provide a workspace export file that contains multiple tenant blobs due to downstream aggregation, BlueNorth will reject it. We need an end-to-end verification step in the export pipeline to validate that only workspace records are included. ETA: +2 sprint points to add validation (approx 6 working days).

2) CMK (customer-managed key) support for exports
- Option A (fast): Provide a downloadable archive that we encrypt locally with the customer's public key before handing it off. Pros: quick, keeps long-term storage unchanged. Cons: requires secure key exchange and adds client-side complexity.
- Option B (full CMK wrap): Integrate export-time KMS wrapping so the object is stored encrypted under the customer's CMK in our bucket. Pros: seamless for customer, consistent. Cons: requires KMS access patterns, entitlement checks, and vault changes; ETA: ~4-6 weeks (infra heavy).

3) SSO / canonical user ID mapping
- We can add a join step to the audit pipeline that writes a canonical_user_id column at write-time by consulting the auth service mapping table. Effort: ~3 working days + a small migration for historical backfill if BlueNorth wants prior 90-day completeness.

Recommendation: For pilot acceptance by Nov 20, deliver (i) workspace-scoped verified exports, (ii) client-encrypted downloadable archive (Option A) as temporary CMK path, and (iii) write-time canonical_user_id for new events. Follow up with full CMK wrap as a tracked infra ticket (SEC-1284).

I'll prepare a short ops checklist and a templated email to BlueNorth. If y'all agree, Priyom can send the pilot acceptance note and we triage SEC-1284 into the December sprint.

Marissa
Group Product Manager, Compliance Integrations
